text: November twenty-fourth, nineteen seventy-one. A calm man in a dark suit buys a plane ticket with cash. Name: Dan Cooper.
On the short flight from Portland to Seattle, he orders a bourbon... and hands the flight attendant a note.
He has a bomb in his briefcase.
He opens it just enough for her to see. Red sticks. Wires. A battery.
His demands: two hundred thousand dollars in twenties, and four parachutes.
In Seattle, he gets the cash, lets all thirty-six passengers go, and sends the plane back into the sky.
Then, at night, in the rain, over the forests of Washington... he lowers the rear stairs and jumps.
With the money. Into the dark. Main character energy, honestly.
The FBI searched for years. No body. No parachute. Nothing.
Then, in nineteen eighty, an eight-year-old boy digging on a Columbia River beach found almost six thousand dollars in rotting twenties. Cooper's money.
The rest of the cash? Never found.
Even his name is a mistake. He called himself Dan Cooper. A reporter's error made him D.B.
In twenty sixteen, the FBI gave up the active hunt.
So... did he die in those woods? Or is D.B. Cooper the man who got away?
